name: wolcott_preflight
one_line: Estimate a task's cost before it starts and stop to ask if it is out of range.
problem: Large jobs start without a price; X1 was planned at 4,134 hours and measured at 463. A cheap estimate and a stop line would have caught that before spending.
design: Before launch, count the units of work (rows, files, phases) and multiply by the measured dollars per unit of the nearest audited task class.
Print the range (low, expected, high) and a stop line at 1.5x expected; the coordinator checks spend at each phase boundary.
At the end, record estimated versus measured cost; the estimate error is itself logged so the estimator improves.
Run as a saver: its value is verified only when a test shows a job stopped or re-scoped early and its measured cost is lower than the unchecked baseline.
inputs: dollars per unit by task class from verified tests and profiles

cost_estimate.basis: a short script plus one extra coordinator turn at each phase boundary
cost_estimate.note: Estimate only (unverified). Never counted as a saving.

first_test: Price the next Y1 phase up front, run it, and compare estimate with measured get_session cost.
risks: A wrong estimate gives false comfort or false alarms; with only 4 complete audited sessions the ranges will be wide.
